plan.notes: Source: official Huntington University 'Computer Science (B.S. Degree) Academic Plan (4-year) 2026-2030' (acad_plan_2026_computer_science_bs.pdf), cross-checked against the official 2026 Computer Science BS checksheet (checksheet_2026_computer_science_bs.pdf); both downloaded from huntington.edu on 2026-09-30. Transcription method: pdftotext layout extraction plus visual verification of every row against the rendered PDF. TRUE degree name confirmed: 'Computer Science (B.S. Degree)'. CREDIT VERIFICATION: every printed term total was checked row-by-row against the listed courses and all match (Fall 2026 = CS111 3 + MA165 3 + EN141 3 + HS____ 3 + HU210 3 + SS111 1 = 16; Spring 2027 = 15; Fall 2027 = 16; Spring 2028 = 15; Fall 2028 = 15; Spring 2029 = 15; Fall 2029 = 14; Spring 2030 = 3 + 9 + 2 = 14; the 3 Immersive Experience milestones are 0-credit). Listed credits sum to 120, equal to the catalog bachelor's minimum ('A minimum of 120 Hours is required for any Bachelor's Degree; 36 of those hours must be Upper-level,' per the 2026 checksheet) and to the plan's own published total of 120. No discrepancy. Plan conventions: underlining = required for major (CS111, MA165, MA150, CS216, CS325, CS275, CS362, CS315, CS425, CS355, CS386, CS415, CS435, CS436); asterisk = alternating-year course (CS325, CS275, CS362, CS315, CS425, CS355, CS386, CS415); superscript 5 = Forester Foundations choice (Historical Perspectives, Social Science, Laboratory Science). Plan notes carried over: (1) satisfactory mathematics placement scores are required before enrolling in math/CS courses (placement policy in Catalog, Academic Information) - placement detail, not an external prereq; (2) MA171 Calculus I may be taken in place of MA150; (3) students are encouraged to minor in cyber security, data analytics, mathematics, business, graphic design, or another application area; (4) a minimum of 36 hours of 300+ courses is required for graduation. The plan prints no course prerequisites, so all prereq fields are empty (prereqs were not invented). Summer terms on the plan are empty. Huntington labels this a 'Typical Program' - actual programs vary. Immersive Experiences (Cultural Enrichment, Creative Arts, Experiential Learning) are 0-credit graduation milestones listed on the plan; included with required_zero:true and attached to Spring Year 4 although they are completed across the degree.
